Subject: Next steps: deployment pathway & sizing for ClearLedger

Hi Maria — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive: 

Summary of your requirements (from call):
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II required; KMS integration for keys; audit logs retained 1 year.
- Target workload: steady-state ~120 TPS (inference requests), peak bursts up to ~300 TPS for short periods.
- Typical token profile: user prompt ~120 tokens, model reply ~420 tokens (avg. total per request ~540 tokens).
- Concurrency target: ~=40 concurrent active requests during peak.
- SLO: P95 latency target <350ms for standard chat flows; some async batch reranking ok.
- Data gravity: customer data must remain in VPC/controlled environment; long-term preference for Private (VPC/on-prem) but open to starting with Dedicated POC to shorten time-to-value.

Initial recommendations (high-level):
1) Start with a Dedicated reserved pool POC (4–6 GPUs) to prove throughput and observe token economics; migrate to Private VPC once baseline SLA/KMS/audit needs are verified.
2) Hardware options to benchmark during POC: H100 (best latency/throughput), A100-80GB (cost-effective for dense models), and a quantized L4-class option for lower-cost burst handling.
3) POC scope: realistic traffic replay (mix of 70% short prompts / 30% long generation), KV prefix caching for repeated system prompts, and autoscaling/burst strategy for peak 300 TPS windows.

Ask from your side to proceed: please confirm the following by EOD if possible:
- Is SOC 2 Type II + KMS integration the full compliance list, or are there additional regs (PCI, regional data residency)?
- Can you share a small sample trace (10–20 anonymized requests) showing token lengths and any large-system prompts?
- Confirm preferred POC start week (we suggested week of Sep 6).

I've attached the capacity worksheet and POC scope draft to fill in the details. Ben and Lauren — see inline for technical asks so we can prepare estimates ahead of the sizing call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Lauren — quick technical notes to prepare for Tue Sep 7 sizing call (pulled from notes + preliminary perf numbers). Posting estimates so we can be crisp on the call: 

Assumptions from Maria's profile: avg total tokens/request = 540; peak concurrency ~40; peak TPS burst 300 (short windows). Target latency P95 <350ms for chat flows.

Model / hardware rough throughput (single-GPU, approximate, avg tokens 540):
- H100 (optimized kernels, int8/amp): ~180–220 TPS per GPU at P95<350ms when using large-seq optimizations and KV cache. For safety, budget 160 TPS for sustained load accounting for variability (so 2–3 H100s could cover steady 120 TPS with headroom; burst handling needs either autoscale or burst pool).
- A100-80GB: ~110–140 TPS per GPU under same model/config. Good cost/perf balance; may need 3–4 GPUs for the steady+headroom scenario.
- L4-class / quantized cost tier: ~30–60 TPS per card (best for small models / reranking offloads).

Sizing guidance for POC to validate:
- Baseline Dedicated pool: 3 x A100-80GB GPUs (covers steady 120 TPS with headroom for autoscale) OR 2 x H100 if they prioritize latency and smaller pod size for testing.
- Burst strategy: enable burst pool (pre-warmed smaller quantized instances) that can absorb short 300 TPS spikes while autoscaler provisions additional capacity.
- Concurrency & batching: set application concurrency target to ~48 (client-side threadpool); runtime batching target 4–8 tokens-per-batch for latency-sensitive flows. KV/prefix caching for system prompts expected to reduce avg cost ~10–20% depending on prompt reuse.
- Quantization notes: INT8 or FP16 quantized 13B-class models can hit ~20–35% cost reduction with careful evals on QA metrics; reranking quality is sensitive, so propose validating with a held-out set during POC.

Action items before Sep 7 sizing call:
- Karthik: confirm which model families they want tested (open to our Redwood-verified 13B and 33B variants?).
- Lauren: can you prepare a short perf-run checklist + recommended profiling commands and a list of perf counters we'll capture (latency histograms, GPU util, memory headroom, batch size distributions)?

I can draft a quick cost / GPU-count table for both A100 and H100 options to present on the call.

- Ben
